thesis_summary.thesis: Dollar General Corporation (NYSE: DG) operates more than **20,000** small-box discount stores in **47** U.S. states, focused on rural and small-town communities where larger retailers are scarce. **[Fact]** FY2025 net sales were **$42.7 billion**, up from **$40.6 billion** in FY2024. **[Fact]** The mix is heavily consumables (food, health and beauty, cleaning), with seasonal, apparel, and home categories filling out the basket. **[Fact]** Stores average roughly **7,400 square feet**, use a low-cost build model, and rely on a centralized distribution network. **[Inference]** Dollar General is a high-turn consumables compounder whose economics depend on store density, purchasing scale, and reliable in-stock execution in price-sensitive markets.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The market may be pricing a **recovery in same-store sales and margin** after shrink and supply-chain problems while underweighting **$4.6 billion of debt** still on the balance sheet and **$1.2 billion of annual capital spending** that already sits between operating cash flow and owner cash. **[Inference]** At **$126.59**, the stock trades below our refreshed proof base value per share, implying the market discounts reinvestment returns or terminal economics versus our bounded base case. **[Fact]** Insider activity over the past year shows modest open-market buying alongside larger planned sales, which weakens a pure "insiders know more" bull case unless those sales are largely 10b5-1 programs.
